fr_defiler_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe beats his drum and leads the ducks in a PARADE – they file past in a line (day-fee-LAY).
fr_defiler_verb.why: Défilé = parade, think 'file past' → défiler = to parade; the mime marches the ducks along the square.

fr_promouvoir_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe PROMOTES the hen to head chef – he hands her a tall white chef's hat in her nest.
fr_promouvoir_verb.why: Promote → promouvoir = to promote; the hen gets a promotion from the mime.

fr_chevaucher_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe RIDES a tiny donkey, his boots nearly dragging – a 'cheval' ride (shuh-voh-SHAY).
fr_chevaucher_verb.why: Cheval = horse → chevaucher = to ride (astride); the mime sits astride the donkey. Text pass 2026-10-28: bracketed respelling matched to the card (sheh-voh-SHAY -> shuh-voh-SHAY).

fr_programmer_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe PROGRAMS his little robot with a remote control to walk the dog – but the dog walks the robot!
fr_programmer_verb.why: Program → programmer = to program; the mime presses the buttons on the remote.

fr_escorter_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe ESCORTS the ducklings safely past the swans, waving a white flag.
fr_escorter_verb.why: Escort → escorter = to escort, accompany; the mime leads the ducklings past the swans.

fr_amorcer_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe BEGINS fishing: he hooks a MORSEL of bread on his line (ah-mor-SAY).
fr_amorcer_verb.why: Morsel / bait → amorcer = to begin (to bait, to start off); the mime starts by baiting the hook.

fr_longer_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe walks ALONG the LONG harbor wall with a blue jay flying beside him (lohn-ZHAY).
fr_longer_verb.why: Long + jay → longer = to go along; the mime walks the length of the wall. Text pass 2026-10-28: bracketed respelling matched to the card (lohn-JAY -> lohn-ZHAY).

fr_ramper_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe CRAWLS on the ROMPER rug after his red ball (rahn-PAY).
fr_ramper_verb.why: Romper → ramper = to crawl; the mime crawls on all fours over the rug. Text pass 2026-10-28: bracketed respelling matched to the card (rahm-PAY -> rahn-PAY).

fr_pointer_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe POINTS AT the squirrel in the tree – and his POINTER dog points too.
fr_pointer_verb.why: Pointer → pointer = to point at; the mime's finger and his dog both point to the squirrel.

fr_rebondir_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe throws the ball and it REBOUNDS off the lamp post – boing!
fr_rebondir_verb.why: Rebound → rebondir = to bounce, rebound (green beret: -ir like finir); the dotted arc shows the bounce.

fr_roder_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe PROWLS round the fish crates with a sly fox – they're up to something (roh-DAY).
fr_roder_verb.why: 'Road-ay' – sneaking along the road → rôder = to prowl; the mime and the fox creep by the crates.

fr_echouer_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe sneezes 'ay-SHOO!' and his toy rocket FAILS – it just fizzles on the ground (ay-shoo-AY).
fr_echouer_verb.why: 'Ay-shoo' sneeze → échouer = to fail; the rocket never takes off.

fr_efforcer_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe STRIVES with great EFFORT to push the giant pumpkin, checking his red face in his mirror.
fr_efforcer_verb.why: Effort → s'efforcer (de) = to strive, try hard; the hand mirror shows it is reflexive (s').

fr_guider_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe GUIDES the little sailing boat in to the jetty – 'G'DAY, this way!' (gee-DAY).
fr_guider_verb.why: Guide → guider = to guide; the mime waves the boat in. Text pass 2026-10-28: bracketed respelling matched to the card (ghee-DAY -> gee-DAY).

fr_naviguer_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe NAVIGATES the harbor in a walnut-shell boat, eye to his telescope.
fr_naviguer_verb.why: Navigate → naviguer = to navigate, sail; the mime steers his nutshell boat.

fr_elancer_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe DASHES FORWARD with his LANCE at the hanging ring (ay-lahn-SAY), his mirror at his belt.
fr_elancer_verb.why: Lance → s'élancer = to dash forward, launch oneself; the hand mirror shows it is reflexive (s').

fr_sursauter_verb.hook: 'SIR, your SAUTÉ!' – the frying pan spits and sizzles and Monsieur Verbe JUMPS with surprise (sewr-soh-TAY).
fr_sursauter_verb.why: Sir + sauté → sursauter = to jump (with surprise); the mime leaps in the air by the pan. Text pass 2026-10-28: bracketed respelling matched to the card (sur-soh-TAY -> sewr-soh-TAY).

fr_ecrouler_verb.hook: The tower of CRUMBLE bowls COLLAPSES and Monsieur Verbe gasps into his mirror (ay-kroo-LAY).
fr_ecrouler_verb.why: Crumble → s'écrouler = to collapse, crumble; the hand mirror shows it is reflexive (s').

fr_effondrer_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe's cart of FONDUE pots is about to COLLAPSE on the path – he stares in his mirror (ay-fohn-DRAY).
fr_effondrer_verb.why: Fondue → s'effondrer = to collapse; the hand mirror shows it is reflexive (s').

fr_cotoyer_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe squeezes onto the bench and RUBS SHOULDERS with two fishermen in their yellow COATS (koh-twah-YAY).
fr_cotoyer_verb.why: Coat-to-coat → côtoyer = to rub shoulders with, mix with; the mime sits shoulder to shoulder with them. Text pass 2026-10-28: bracketed respelling matched to the card (koh-twa-YAY -> koh-twah-YAY).

fr_faufiler_verb.hook: With his FAUX FEELERS on, Monsieur Verbe WORMS HIS WAY between the cows, mirror in hand (foh-fee-LAY).
fr_faufiler_verb.why: Faux feelers → se faufiler = to worm one's way, slip through; the hand mirror shows it is reflexive (se).

fr_aboutir_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe breaks the ribbon – he REACHES the end and SUCCEEDS, waving a BOOT for the donkey (ah-boo-TEER).
fr_aboutir_verb.why: 'A boot' → aboutir = to lead to, to succeed (green beret: -ir like finir); the mime breaks the finish ribbon.

fr_orienter_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe turns his map to the ORIENT – he ORIENTS it with his compass.
fr_orienter_verb.why: Orient → orienter = to orientate, set to north; the mime lines up the map with the compass.

fr_errer_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe WANDERS with no plan – his footprints loop round and round in ERROR (eh-RAY).
fr_errer_verb.why: Error / errant → errer = to wander; the looping footprints show he wanders.

fr_osciller_verb.hook: The big fan OSCILLATES from side to side and Monsieur Verbe's scarf flaps back and forth.
fr_osciller_verb.why: Oscillate → osciller = to oscillate, wobble; the mime watches the fan swing.

fr_derouler_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe UNROLLS the red carpet for a hopping kangaroo – DAY-ROO! (day-roo-LAY).
fr_derouler_verb.why: 'Day-roo' (kangaroo) → dérouler = to unroll; the mime rolls out the carpet.

fr_balader_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe takes a STROLL by the water, humming a BALLAD, while his three ducks waddle along nearby (bah-lah-DAY).
fr_balader_verb.why: Ballad → balader = to take for a stroll (se balader = to go for a stroll); the ducks waddle after the mime. No mirror: here it is the plain verb.
ex: Il balade ses canards au bord de l'eau.
He takes his ducks for a stroll by the water.

fr_transporter_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe TRANSPORTS a crate of oranges with his little harbor crane.
fr_transporter_verb.why: Transport → transporter = to transport, carry; the crane carries the crate to the cart.

fr_ficher_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe FILES his papers in the cabinet – but a FISH is filed in there too (fee-SHAY)!
fr_ficher_verb.why: 'Fish-ay' → ficher = to file; the mime files cards in the fishy drawer.
ex: Elle fiche les noms des clients.
